body:
Three readings now sit on the table, and none can be confirmed from the material: (1) ambiguity in what agreements specified, (2) renegotiation or legitimacy problems under changed circumstances, and (3) divergent views about what kind of household the flat is. The objection is right that the original account's test—whether tightened specifications reduce recurrence—does not distinguish these. The rival is right that avoidance could signal resistance to the form of obligation itself, not just vague terms. But the original account's practical moves still have value if reframed as probes rather than solutions.

What I would keep from the original account: the advice to start with two or three concrete recurring items, to write down what counts as done and when, and to approach the withdrawing flatmate separately with a narrower ask. These remain useful because they are low-cost and reversible. What I would revise: the sequencing and the interpretation of results. Falling recurrence on specified items would not confirm the ambiguity hypothesis; it would only show that specification reduces friction on those items. Rising or displaced recurrence would not refute ambiguity; it would show that specification alone is insufficient.

What I would add from the rival: before or alongside specifying chores, ask each flatmate separately what they take the household to be. This need not be a formal conversation; it can be woven into the separate approach to the withdrawing flatmate. "I'm trying to figure out what would make this workable for everyone. Do you see the flat as a shared project with mutual obligations, or more as three lives overlapping?" The answer matters because it determines whether a specification document feels like clarification or like coercion.

What I would add from the objection: treat the thinness of the material as a reason to keep all three readings live, not as a reason to pick one and sequence remedies around it. The original account's step 5—asking whether the living arrangement still works—should arrive not after specification fails, but after the diagnostic conversations reveal whether the flatmates can agree on what kind of agreement they are making.

What I would leave open: which reading is correct, whether the withdrawing flatmate is acting in good faith, and whether written agreements are appropriate for this household. The strongest claim I can make is that the practical moves in the original account become more informative if they are treated as probes into which reading applies, rather than as a solution to a problem whose nature is already settled.

A household in active conflict may need a single working hypothesis to test, not parallel diagnostics.","bearing":"If actionability matters more than diagnostic precision, the original account's sequencing may be preferable despite its weaker evidential basis."},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Ask each flatmate separately what they take the household to be before or alongside specifying chores.","action":"Separate conversations asking whether the flat is a shared project with mutual obligations or three overlapping private lives.","consequence":"Surfaces the axis the original account does not address; may delay practical relief but increases diagnostic value.","depends":["c1"]},{"id":"u2","type":"use","text":"Treat the original account's specification steps as information-gathering probes, not as confirmation of the ambiguity hypothesis.","action":"Implement two or three concrete specifications and observe whether recurrence falls, rises, or displaces to new items.","consequence":"Provides data to distinguish among the three readings rather than confirming one."},{"id":"p1","type":"problem","text":"The material does not say whether the withdrawing flatmate would engage with a conversation about household type, or whether that conversation would feel coercive to them.","mentions":["u1","c1"]},{"id":"p2","type":"problem","text":"If the three flatmates hold divergent views about household type, there may be no chore arrangement that satisfies all three without one or more accepting a reading they do not hold.","mentions":["c1","u1"]}],"uptake":["c1","c2","c3","u1","u2"]}
